intro.title: Welcome to Errachidia — oasis on the road to the dunes
intro.p1: Errachidia is the administrative capital of the Drâa-Tafilalet region in southeastern Morocco. It sits on the edge of the Tafilalet oasis belt, with the Ziz Valley, palm groves and the road south toward Erfoud and Merzouga.
intro.p2: Travellers often stop for a night between the High Atlas (Midelt) and the dunes: stock up, rest, and see the gorge and palm country before or after the desert. The town itself is functional rather than a long sightseeing destination.

ziz.title: Ziz Valley & Gorge
ziz.p1: The Ziz Valley is the natural corridor that links the Middle Atlas approaches to the Tafilalet. Near Errachidia, the gorge and riverside palm strips make for a striking drive and short stops at viewpoints.
ziz.p2: Best experienced by car or taxi with time to pull over. Early morning or late afternoon light is softer on the cliffs and palms.
ziz.tip: Combine with a palm-grove walk the same day if you have a vehicle.

palmeraie.title: Palm groves
palmeraie.p1: Palm groves around Errachidia are the green heart of the oasis — date palms, irrigation channels and small plots that define Tafilalet agriculture.
palmeraie.p2: Walk where paths are open and respect private plots. The contrast between oasis green and the surrounding dry hills is the classic southeastern landscape.
palmeraie.tip: Shade is welcome in the middle of the day; carry water.

centre.title: Town centre & souk
centre.p1: Errachidia's centre is practical: shops, cafés, transport and a local souk rather than a polished tourist medina.
centre.p2: Use it to restock, eat and organise onward travel. Market days bring more energy — ask locally which day is busiest.
centre.tip: Good base for a coffee after the gorge drive.

ksour.title: Nearby ksour
ksour.p1: The wider Tafilalet still holds traditional ksour — fortified adobe villages that once protected oasis communities and trade routes.
ksour.p2: Some are lived-in; others are partly abandoned. Visit with respect and, where possible, a local guide for context.
ksour.tip: Often combined with the road toward Erfoud or Rissani.

oasis_life.title: Oasis life
oasis_life.p1: Dates, irrigation and seasonal work still shape daily life around Errachidia. The oasis is not a museum — it is a working landscape.
oasis_life.p2: Buying local dates and observing water channels is a simple way to connect with the region without a long programme.
oasis_life.tip: Autumn and winter are more comfortable for walking in the open sun.

south_road.title: Road south to Erfoud
south_road.p1: From Errachidia the road continues south toward Erfoud and the Erg Chebbi dunes (Merzouga area). Many desert tours start or pass here.
south_road.p2: Allow time for the drive; conditions can be hot and dry. For dune camps and Erg Chebbi details, use Merzouga place pages.
south_road.tip: Stock water and fuel before long desert stretches.

q1.question: How long should I stay in Errachidia?
q1.answer: One night is common as a transit stop; two nights if you want a slower gorge and palm-grove day.

q2.question: Is Errachidia close to Merzouga?
q2.answer: About 2–2.5 hours by road toward Erfoud then the dunes. Errachidia is a gateway, not the dune camp itself.

q3.question: How do I get to Errachidia?
q3.answer: By road from Midelt (north) or Erfoud (south), or via Errachidia airport (ERH) when flights operate.

q4.question: What is the Ziz Gorge?
q4.answer: A scenic stretch of the Ziz Valley near Errachidia — cliffs, river and palms — best seen by vehicle with short stops.

itinerary.title: Suggested 2–3 Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan for the Ziz, palms and the road toward the dunes.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Drive the Ziz corridor with stops at viewpoints. Soft morning light works well on cliffs and palms.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Restock, café and a short walk through the practical centre and souk area.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Simple tagine or grill and an early night before another desert-edge day.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Walk oasis paths where open, watch irrigation channels and the contrast with dry hills.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Visit a traditional ksar with respect; a local guide adds useful context if available.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Dates, tea and a hearty plate before deciding south or north the next day.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Fuel, water and a final café. Confirm road conditions if heading toward the dunes.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: South toward Erfoud and Erg Chebbi (see Merzouga pages for camps), or north toward Midelt and the Atlas.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Overnight in Erfoud, a dune camp, or back toward the Atlas depending on your route.
